title: Why Does Garlic Breath Last 24 Hours? 🧄
description:
Why does garlic breath last so long? One garlic gas, allyl methyl sulfide, isn't broken down by your gut or liver, so it travels in your blood and comes out through your lungs and sweat for up to a day, which is why mouthwash can't fix it.

Sources:
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9950816/
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garlic_breath

topic: Why does garlic breath last a whole day?
script:
Your garlic breath can leak out of your lungs for twenty-four hours. Why?
Mouthwash won't stop it.
Crush a clove of garlic
and it lets off a bunch of stinky sulfur gases.
Most break down fast.
But one is sneaky.
It's called allyl methyl sulfide.
Your gut and liver barely touch it,
so it slips into your blood
and rides around your whole body.
Each time that blood passes through your lungs,
a little leaks out on your breath.
Some even sneaks out through your sweat.
Three hours after dinner,
it's the main garlic smell you're breathing out.
And it keeps that up for hours and hours.
Raw apple, mint or milk can help a little.
So really,
garlic breath is garlic blood.
Would you still eat garlic before a date?
key_facts: Crushed garlic releases several volatile sulfur compounds; allyl methyl sulfide (AMS) is the one that lingers (Suarez et al. 1999; PopSci/Barringer)
AMS is barely metabolized by the gut and liver, so it is absorbed into the blood and exhaled through the lungs; also excreted via skin and urine (PubMed 9950816; Wikipedia)
About 3 hours after eating garlic, AMS was the main sulfur gas on the breath (Suarez et al. 1999)
Garlic can still be smelled on the breath about 24 hours later (Sheryl Barringer, Ohio State, via PopSci)
Mouthwash and mints don't help much because the compounds come from the blood (Wikipedia)
Raw apple, mint and milk reduce garlic breath volatiles (Ohio State studies, via PopSci/Wikipedia)
